t: core/src/lib.rs is the metaviewer-core crate root: forbid(unsafe_code); public modules admission, catalog, control, guest_command, headless, journal, record, rewind_flow, supervisor, verify, replay, transport, wire, serve. rewind.rs is NOT a module here; only tests/rewind.rs compiles it through #[path].

metaviewer-core binary: reads JSON Config from the file named by MV_CORE_CONFIG, refuses "core component version pin mismatch" when config.core.hello.component_version differs from the compiled CARGO_PKG_VERSION, validates for the effective uid, binds $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/metaviewer/core.sock, opens Server on serve::state_dir() and serves on a current-thread tokio runtime.

metaviewer-core exits with status 2 and prints "metaviewer-core: <error>" on any startup error: MV_CORE_CONFIG required, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR required, version pin mismatch, config validation, bind or Server::open failure.

mv-replay is the offline journal verifier: mv-replay --journal <journal.jsonl> --witness-root <session dir> [--anchor <file>] [--verify-only]. It calls journal::scan (or anchor::scan_with_anchor) and prints the sha256 of the replayed CoreState snapshot unless --verify-only. Any repeated, unknown or missing argument is JournalError::Invalid.

mv-replay exit codes: 0 verified; 3 JournalError::Duplicate (repeated msg_id or core_seq out of order); 4 JournalError::Witness (artifact missing or digest mismatch); 2 everything else, including Invalid, Io, Corrupt(empty|blank|utf8_bom|missing_lf|oversize), Unsealed, Policy and UPGRADE-REQUIRED. The error Display text goes to stderr.

Why mv-replay says Invalid for a relative, symlinked or copied session path: scan() first runs confined(path), which returns Invalid on any ".." component or any symlink along the path, then private_archive(root), which needs root to have two parent directories (state/sessions/<id>) and requires state, sessions, root, events and artifacts each to be a directory owned by the effective uid with mode exactly 0700, else Invalid. A plain recursive copy usually gets a umask mode such as 0755 (inference: depends on the copy tool).

journal/mod.rs is the durable session archive (metaviewer.journal/v1 header line, metaviewer.archive/v1 genesis.json, events/ and artifacts/ sidecars, checkpoint.json with schema metaviewer.checkpoint/v1 binding count, tail, archive and genesis). Every accepted authority transition is one appended SessionRecord whose prev_sha256 chains to the previous tail.

Journal ceilings: whole journal and any artifact at most MAX_BYTES = 64 MiB, at most MAX_RECORDS = 100000 records, one line at most MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 1048576 bytes. Witness caches bounded: MAX_UNCOMMITTED_ARTIFACTS 32, MAX_DIRTY_FILES 32, MAX_VERIFIED_WITNESS_CACHE 256, MAX_SURFACE_WITNESS_BYTES 64 MiB per surface set.

JournalError variants: Invalid, Io, Corrupt, Empty, Blank, Utf8Bom, MissingLf, Oversize, Duplicate, Witness, Unsealed, Policy, Locked, Poisoned, UpgradeRequired{expected,found}. Display gives "Corrupt(<cause>): ..." for the five corruption causes and an UPGRADE-REQUIRED sentence telling the user to archive the session directory unchanged and start a fresh session; others print their Debug name.

Journal full: Journal::append returns JournalError::Policy when count reaches MAX_RECORDS or when the next line would push the journal past MAX_BYTES. The live core does not crash: Server::route_at catches that Policy and calls end_full_journal, which ends admission for the session (see serve/journal_end.rs). The user sees the session end and must start a fresh one for a long run.

Journal::append replays before writing: it re-applies the input to its own copy of CoreState and refuses Invalid unless the outcome and the snapshot equal what the caller computed, and unless outcome.core_seq and state.core_seq are exactly count+1. A poisoned handle (earlier fsync error, inline or background) refuses every later append with Poisoned.

Journal::create starts a session archive: session_id must pass safe_component (1..128 bytes of [A-Za-z0-9._-], not "." or "..") and core_seq must be 0; it makes <state>/sessions/<id>/{events,artifacts} with mode 0700, writes genesis.json and the header line with an exclusive writer lock, writes the first checkpoint and fsyncs directory entries up to the first existing ancestor. A CreationGuard rolls the directory back on failure.

Journal::recover reopens an existing session under the writer lock: if scan fails it tries try_rollback_uncommitted_tail and scans again, so a torn or unsealed tail is rolled back to the durable committed prefix rather than replayed. A checkpoint.next that is not a regular file is Invalid.

journal::scan refusals, in order: confined and private_archive (Invalid), not a file (Corrupt), length 0 (Empty), over 64 MiB (Oversize), header schema not metaviewer.journal/v1 or unsafe session_id (Corrupt), header core_version not this build (UpgradeRequired), genesis schema/header digest/session/core_seq mismatch (Corrupt), more than 100000 records (Policy), repeated msg_id or core_seq not equal to the running count (Duplicate).

A journal written by one core version is never replayed or migrated by another: scan compares header.core_version with CARGO_PKG_VERSION and returns UpgradeRequired. A release bump therefore makes old session journals unreplayable by the new mv-replay; keep the matching binary to audit an old session.

Frame witness verification (verify_surface_frame_with_geometry): refuses Poisoned on a poisoned journal, Witness when expected_len is 0 or over 64 MiB or the digest is not 64 lowercase hex, Witness when the file length differs. An unchanged-frame fast path may reuse the in-memory witness by memcmp, but disk bytes are never marked verified without computing SHA-256.

admission/mod.rs is the single reducer for authority state: CoreState.apply(&Input) is pure and deterministic, so the journal can replay it from genesis. Authority wraps CoreState and Journal; apply_with_witnesses computes the next state on a clone, appends it to the journal, and only then replaces the in-memory state, so a failed write leaves state unchanged.

Authority::admit turns an outcome into action_verdict/v0.2: decision "admitted" with core_seq, or decision "refused" with reason_code from Refusal (STALE_FRAME, SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED, LOCKED_BY_OTHER, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, OUT_OF_BOUNDS, POLICY). The refusal is itself journalled; only a journal error is returned as Err.

Proposal admission check order (CoreState::check): surface in a human role -> POLICY; unknown surface or no frame -> STALE_FRAME; not agent_controlled, not live, or sender not owner -> SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED; refresh pending or based_on_frame sha256/generation differs -> STALE_FRAME; lease held on same surface or same display -> LOCKED_BY_OTHER; zero budget, bad or passed deadline -> BUDGET_EXCEEDED; wait ms over budget.max_ms -> BUDGET_EXCEEDED; scroll dx/dy outside i32 -> OUT_OF_BOUNDS; scroll or wait otherwise -> POLICY; click x/y outside frame or bad expectation bbox -> OUT_OF_BOUNDS; wrong epoch, epoch 0 or sender not Agent -> POLICY.

Replay protection in admission: a proposal is refused POLICY as duplicate when its proposal_id, envelope msg_id or nonce was already seen for that sender, or its seq is not above the last seq. A duplicate is still journalled as a refusal, but does not update the seen sets. An admitted proposal consumes one unit of remaining_budget and takes the surface lease.

Dispatch recheck: Input::Dispatch reruns check with dispatch=true; an unknown proposal_id, or one already dispatched or unknown, is POLICY. A failed recheck removes the pending entry, so the agent must get a new frame-bound admission; the spent budget unit is not refunded.

Capsule slot requests (reduce_slot_request): sender not Ui -> POLICY; reused operation_id with a different request -> POLICY (identical replay returns the earlier result); 256 retained slot outcomes -> POLICY; credential_copy_confirmed false, copy without destination or destination on non-copy, destination equal to source, profile busy, or a profile id starting "mv-" -> POLICY; zero budget -> BUDGET_EXCEEDED.

AdmissionRequest::decode binds a proposal to its peer: it decodes the envelope with closed decoding (OutOfBounds for size limits, InvalidInput otherwise) and requires envelope.from == authenticated peer, session_id == the session, to.component == Core and body ActionProposal; on replay Input::Propose decodes the raw text again and requires the same envelope.
Wire limits used by the core: MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 1048576 per frame, MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES = MAX_FRAME_BYTES - 1, default depth 32, 256 keys, 65536-byte strings.

ReplayTable (replay/mod.rs) records authenticated sender nonces per session: InvalidIdentity when session_id, sender instance or nonce is empty or over 128 chars; ZeroSequence for seq 0; DuplicateNonce for a seen nonce; NonIncreasingSequence when seq is not above the last (except on record_reconnect, which restarts the sequence rail but keeps nonces); Exhausted on u64 overflow; CapacityExceeded at max_entries. new(0) is LimitError::MissingOrZero.

rewind_flow.rs is the live REWIND reducer used by serve/rewind.rs: it tracks one target workload (workload_id, owner_id, generation, authority_epoch), one pending request and the session phase. It never invents physical evidence (PID, mapping, closure); those come from the registered daemon as rewind_event/v0.2.

REWIND submit codes (rewind_flow submit_inner): OWNER when the caller is neither the guest-command creator UI nor the session agent, or the guest owner/workload differ from the target; UNAVAILABLE with no guest command session; BUSY when the guest is not held, has pending commands or a running/cancelling/unknown job, or phase does not fit the op; STALE when params workload_id/generation/authority_epoch differ from the target; DUPLICATE for a repeated request_id or 256 requests; CAPACITY when two points are held with active references or counters overflow; POINT_UNAVAILABLE when restore names no usable point with the session compatibility_sha256; INVALID for a missing field or unknown op.

REWIND phase rules: pause needs ready; resume needs paused; mark needs ready or paused; restore needs paused or recoverable (recoverable only to last_good_usable). resume, restore and mark-from-ready bump generation and authority_epoch. At most two points: a third mark evicts the oldest point with zero active references. point_id is "point-" + sha256 over length-prefixed session id, workload id and request id. A pending request expires after 35 s (deadline_ns = now + 35_000_000_000).
While a REWIND request is pending, unknown or stopping, State::allows_command is false, so guest commands are fenced; commands run again only when the rewind session is empty or in phase ready.

serve/rewind.rs routes rewind_request/v0.2 from authenticated UI or agent peers and answers refusals as rewind_event/v0.2 with event "refused" and data {op, code}; the session snapshot is included only for the agent or the guest-command creator.

rewind.rs is a standalone pure REWIND reducer, intentionally not registered in the live core; it is compiled only by core/tests/rewind.rs. Its synthetic structs are test inputs, never physical witnesses. Read rewind_flow.rs for live behaviour.

record/mod.rs is the recording authority seam: the caller supplies admitted surface ids and a durable JournalSink; a sink failure commits neither recording state nor the chain cursor. Entries carry metadata only, raw pixels never cross the sink. EXPORT_BYTE_LIMIT = 16 MiB is shared by exporter and receipt admission.

Recording request refusals (record handle): POLICY "surface is not admitted", POLICY "recording is not active in this mode and surface", POLICY "recording bounds are invalid", BUDGET_EXCEEDED "recording exceeds configured limits" or a held-reservation detail, POLICY "recording identity was already used", POLICY "host destination is not authorized".

RAM capture limits (record/capture.rs): at most 64 retained captures, 8 active recordings, 8 MiB per ring, 64 MiB total retained pixel bytes, max_fps ceiling 60 and default 3 fps with period decimation.

Capture prepare refusals: NOT_RECORDING (recordStop on an id that is not an active recording), SURFACE_UNKNOWN (surface not admitted), ALREADY_RECORDING (surface already has an active recording), CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE (no latest frame for the surface yet), LIMIT (64 rows, 8 active, or retained bytes plus this frame over 64 MiB).

Recording export refusals: CAPTURE_UNKNOWN, NOT_SEALED (export before stop sealed it), CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE (pixels gone), LIMIT (archive over 16 MiB), DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE (destination directory cannot be pinned, created or re-verified).

read_published_frame accepts a frame only from /dev/shm: the path must already be canonical (no symlink, no ".."), a regular file owned by the core effective uid with no group or other permission bits, exact byte length, the same device and inode before, during and after the read, and valid RGB geometry; otherwise "invalid frame witness".

verify/mod.rs is core-owned verification of action receipts over frame-bound evidence, independent of model inference; called only after admission epoch and lease gates; missing evidence refuses. MAX_RGB_BYTES = 256 MiB bounds reads of untrusted frame paths.

serve/journal_end.rs handles the journal capacity end: a capacity refusal ends admission, not transport. Accepted records flush before peers are told; a metaviewer.journal-ended/v1 marker (core_seq, state_sha256) is renamed into place as journal-ended.json and checked on load (regular file, at most 1024 bytes, owned by the effective uid, no group/other bits). Remaining live surfaces get emergency destroy commands, one at a time.
